title: OpenCV camera service with device enumeration and lifecycle
description: Implement camera/camera_service.py to discover available camera devices, capture frames in a background thread, maintain bounded queues, and release hardware resources cleanly on stop/shutdown.
acceptanceCriteria: Discovers available camera indices on Windows/Linux
Starts and stops camera capture on a background worker thread
Provides latest frame safely to consumers without blocking camera capture
Properly releases cv2.VideoCapture on stop or exception to prevent device locks
Supports synthetic/test frame generator mode when camera is unavailable
Unit tests verify lifecycle transitions and safe resource release

steps.description: Create CameraService skeleton and thread worker
steps.details: Create camera/camera_service.py with CameraService class managing a background threading.Thread for cv2.VideoCapture loop.
Implement list_available_cameras() testing device indices (0..3) with fast timeouts, returning list of valid device indices.
Implement thread-safe frame access with bounded queue / latest frame reference; implement start(camera_index) and stop() with cv2.VideoCapture.release().
When use_mock=True or when no camera is present, generate realistic test frames with simulated faces for automated test runs.
Create tests/test_camera_service.py covering initialization, start, stop, mock capture, and clean release.

technicalNotes: Run inference outside camera capture thread to avoid dropping camera frames.
Handle cv2.VideoCapture releasing thoroughly in try/finally blocks.
